Mhlengi Gwala Brutal Attack [5194]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Further information:
On the 6th of March at 3:30 am triathlete Hlengi Gwala, was cycling near the University of KwaZulu-Natal (Howard College Campus) when he was brutally attacked by 3 men who attempted to cut off his leg with a hacksaw.

His friend and training partner, Sandile Shange explained how the horrific incident took place.
“He was cycling up the hill towards UKZN when he was stopped by the three men. They began dragging him towards the bushes and he thought they were trying to rob him so he offered his iPhone and his Garmin watch to the men. He was speaking in Zulu and pleading with the men to take the bicycle and his valuables but he realised they were speaking a different African language. The pulled him into the bushes and pulled out a hacksaw. They then tried to cut one of his leg’s off.


“They were using it manually and they cut deep into one of his legs until they hit the bone and the saw got stuck. He was screaming for help the whole time. A passing security vehicle disturbed the men who ran off and Mhlengi managed to crawl out of the bushes and flag down the security. He is currently in Chief Albert Luthuli Hospital where he is recovering. The doctors will examine him again on Wednesday. The blood flow is good at the moment and he is able to move his toes which is a positive sign,” Shange said.

Durban North Olympic medallist, Henri Schoeman, who knows Gwala, said he was horrified by the incident.
“When I first heard the news, my heart sunk and I couldn’t comprehend how something like that could even be possible. As a cyclist, road safety is something very close to my heart. I wish Mhlengi all the best in his operation today and I hope he makes a full recovery. I know that he’s got tons of support here in Durban to help him through this tough time,” he told the Northglen News.
Schoeman also took to Twitter to express his disgust at the attack.

We will be able to speak to Hlengi, his mother, his coach and the doctors who are looking after him.

Press Release:


Mhlengi Gwala: Road to Recovery
When three assailants stopped triathlete Mhlengi Gwala during his late night training session, little did he know that the brutal chainsaw attack which followed would change his life forever. Now after multiple surgeries to save his legs, Gwala has begun the long road to recovery. Doctors believe it could take up to two years before he’s fully back on his feet, and even then, there are no guarantees that he will ever be able to race again. Carte Blanche meets this remarkable survivor.


Script:


Chainsaw Script


Mlengi
I was trying to fight and I was crying and screaming. And see that chainsaw like rolling and going to my leg.

Link
It was in the wee hours of the morning when 27 year old triathlete ,Mhlengi Gwala who was perparing for the Bloemfontein championships, was brutally attacked by 3 men who pulled him into the bushes.

V/O
Mhlengi Gwala and Sandile Shange are best friends and have been triathlete training partners for 5 years.

Link
Mhlengi was introduced to becoming a triathlete by his friend Sandile Shange, they both worked as life guards on these Durban Beaches.

Sandile
I noticed him when he won his long run in SA champs in 2013, and he liked my swimming cause he was not a good swimmer. He came to approach me to say “hey, its my first time to see an african guy swim as fast as you do”, and I said “actually I do traithlon and I think your running can be better if you come across to try triathlon”, and then he gave it a try, and he was hooked.

Link
Mhlengi had a very promising career. He took part in 3 world championships and was set to compete in the world championships in September this year.

V/O
But these dreams have now been shattered.
Mlengi was cycling to meet Sandile the morning of the attack, so that they could train together.

Mhlengi
I was cycling from my house to the beach where I am used to training, then suddenly there are 3 guys they came, out of the bush, they great me and ask me where I am going to train and then they pull a gun and take me to the bush.

Sandile
He thought it was a robbery , he offered him the phone they did not want to take it, he offered them his watch, they didn’t want that, and he thought they wanted to go into the bushes and take his bike.





V/O
Although he is in extreme pain, Mhlenge agreed to tell us his story from his hospital bed. When the men forced him off the road, robbery did not seem the motive.

Mlenghi
And then they were talking like themselves, a language I did not understand it. And then the one was holding me at the back and the other one the feet and then they start to cut my leg. And then I try to scream and roll and try to fight them.

Sandile
Maybe he thought they were scaring him with the chainsaw and then the other guy started cutting him.

Nlanhla
Tell us about your pain?

Mhlengi
Yo, it was pain pain pain, I was thinking that I am dying, it was very painful.

Sandile
He thought they were killing him. He though they were going to held him and start cutting and then next minute these two guys were sitting on his upper body and the other guy was going straight for his legs.

V/O
But something disturbed them.

Mhlenge
He stopped the chainsaw and then he go back to check and then he said let’s go guys and then they just went. Try to call the police they did not answer, I phoned Sandile and he did not answer and then I think I will die sitting and then I have to try to walk back to the road.

Link
Luckily for Mhlengi a fidelity guard saw light in the bushes and went to investigate.

Mhlengi
Saw in the road I own my light waited any car that was coming I would try to flash and stop it and lucky it work.

V/O
Dumi was doing his nightly rounds as a Fidelity Security Inspector and saw Mhlengi’s light.

Dumi
Luckily God gave him the power to limp the road.



V/O
In all the years that he has been patrolling Dumi says that he has never seen an incident like this before. As the only eye witness, he has asked for his identity to be hidden.

Dumi
And then I saw the light waving on me. Ok then I stop the man just open the door and jump in my car. And then he said don’t even ask what is happening. Please my man I am dying take me to hospital.

V/O
He put his hazards on and raced him there.

Mhlengi
Security did not notice I am injured, maybe he thought I have cramp or something. When he took me out at Albert Lithuli he saw I was very very injured.

Dumi
And then I tried to pick up the man to the wheelchair and then that is where I realised the man was badly injured.

Nhlanhla
How deep were the cuts to his legs

Dumi
Ay my man that thing was very very deep. For me I thought that the leg ws cut off but I realise when I put him in a wheel chair, the bone is not cut off because the leg hanging like this. But it was very deep from side to side.Because the blood that was on the floor was like I was slaughtering a goat.

V/O
The nurses at Inhkosi Albert Lithuli Hospital called Sandile and told him to rush to the hospital to help his friend.

Sandile
When I saw his leg, it’s look like someone just took his leg into the butchery and cut it, it was ridiculous.

V/O
Plastic Surgeon Dr O’Sharran Singh was on duty when Mhlenge was transferred to Saint Augustine’s. He and a team of doctors spent 5 and a half hours trying to repair his nerves and muscles with microsurgery.

Dr Singh
We found that he did have good blood supply of one of the three vessels left in his lower leg and so fo us it was a relief. The unfortunate part of the history was that about 80% of the leg was severed. The chain saw lacerated through his posterior compartment through the muscles and went to all the way and sent all the way to the bone. It went through about 90% of that also.

V/O
The orthopedic surgeon used metal pins to secure the bone.
Mhlengi was millimeters away from loosing his leg .

Mlenge
Only 20 % is holding the leg. But it’s a miracle today because I saw my leg and it looks normal I just need to heal.

Link
Police are investigating but the motive is still unclear. Was it jealousy or was it a muti attack?

Sandile
When he told me it was not a robbery. He tried to offer them a watch, a phone a bicycle, they were not interested in that but the only thing they were interested in was to cut his feet.


Mhlengi
Many things happen in South Africa, people they do mad things, I don’t have any enemies, I am smiling for everybody. I talk with everybody. I don’t know I really don’t.

Sandile
So we were trying to find out what was the cause and until today we are still puzzled.


Sue
A nicer person it couldn’t have happened to. We don’t know if it was an isolated incident that he just happened to be at the wrong place at the wrong time. We just don’t know.At this stage we are flabbergasted to be honest.

V/O
It’s a tight knit community of triathletes in Durban, Sue de la Porte’s family is very involved in the sport and she helps and mentors Sandile and Hlenge where she can.

Sue
One the Tuesday I lost all hope in humanity and by the Thursday it was back.

Link
The public response has been phenominal , a crowd funding initiative called “Get Mhlengi back on his bike” has been created and funds are flowing in.



Sandile

I am over courage. I thought it was something that was going to be his friends and family and colleagues but it seems like it has touched everyone all over the world. We’ve been getting messages from china from bbc news london. I will just say thank you to everyone.

Sue
It is just such a shocking bizarre thing to happen that I think globally ity’s just grabbed people’s attention and theya re shocked so they have come in and offered support in any way they can.

V/O
But the big question is, will he ever be able to compete again?

Nhlanhla
What is the prognosis?

Dr Singh
Mhlengi doing really well. In terms of a career as a professional athete have to access and reveal its itself next year to two years.

Sue
“We are focussing hugely on keeping him positive, I think its so important for him. He’s a fighter and he said to me , I need crutches and I said slowly this is going to be a slow process, you know each day is going to take time. The next day he had crutches he is just that kind of guy.

V/O
Thankfully due to the generosity of the public, his extensive medical bills will be covered and he will be able to get help and support he needs.

Mhlenge
I think I’m doing good. My leg can move, my toes can move,up and down . Doctor said cycling and swimming do it easily but running take long to do it.

Nhlanhla
Hopefully still be a triathlete

Mhlengi

Ya for sure I will I will.

Imagine being conscious and feeling a chainsaw cutting through the flesh and bone of your leg, this is what SA Champion Triathelete Mlengi Gwala experienced in Durban when 3 men pulled him off his bike and took him to the bushes.

“He thought they were killing him and then the other guy started to cut his legs.”

V/O
With 3 world championships under his belt 27 year old traithelete Mhlengi Gwala had a very promising career. But these dreams were shattered when 3 men held him down and tried to cut off his leg with a chainsaw.

Triathlete Mhlengi Gwala was viciously attacked when 3 men pulled him off his bike and tried to cut off his legs with a chainsaw. He was within millimeters of loosing his leg, but is determined to compete again.
“I was thinking that I am dying, it was very painful.”

V/O
When three robbers stopped triathlete Mhlengi Gwala during his late night training session, little did he know that the brutal chainsaw attack which followed, would change his life forever.

“And then I try to scream and roll and try to fight them.”
